name: The O'Leary barn

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: Standing on the night of the fire (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 707-715); when it was built is not known, and the scene's phase begins in 1860.

change_note: Built T-3689 (2026-11-20): the O'Leary site on DeKoven Street, on the landmark_1871 archetype in the 1835 town's clapboard and shingles.

placement.position_note: At the rear of lot 137 on the north alley, 175 feet along Andreas's line from the block's north-east corner (vol. 2, p. 711); its south side eight feet north of the rear of Dalton's house next door and about forty feet behind the cottages (the 'forty-foot yard'), so its north side falls on the alley line. The footprint's origin is local E -321.39 N -1930.04.
placement.symbolic_location: At the rear of 137 DeKoven Street, on the north alley.

footprint.note: Sixteen by twenty feet (Andreas vol. 2, p. 711), the long side running back from the street.

blocks.name: the barn
blocks.note: 'A small wooden barn, sixteen by twenty feet, and fourteen feet high' with a loft above, 'recently filled with hay' (the Board's report and Andreas vol. 2, pp. 708-711); its cows, a calf and a horse stood below. Its doors are reconstructed: a man door from the yard and a wagon door on the alley, as the O'Learys kept a horse and wagon.

fire.note: The fire began in the barn, between 8:45 and 9:30 on Sunday evening (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 708, 719; the Board of Police and Fire Commissioners): it burned to the ground.

value.note: THE O'LEARY BARN, built by T-3689 for the 1871 scene: a frame barn sixteen by twenty feet and fourteen feet high at the rear of the O'Leary lot on the north alley, a hayloft over five cows, a calf and a horse, where the fire began between 8:45 and 9:30 on the evening of Sunday 8 October 1871 (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 707-715). No picture of it is known: it burned that night.

composition.note: Sizes from Andreas's account where he gives them; storeys, roofs and openings from the photograph where it shows them, else reconstructed as the neighbourhood's one-storey frame cottages.

wall_material.value: Sawn boards on a frame, a shingle roof
wall_material.note: A wooden barn (Andreas); its boarding and roof are reconstructed as the neighbourhood's.

function.note: A barn and stable for the O'Learys' cows and horse (Andreas vol. 2, p. 708).

built.note: Not known: reconstructed as the cottages' decade.

citations.citation: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time. Vol. 2, From 1857 until the Fire of 1871. Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1885.
